dedupe_keys.name: aws post event summaries of major service disruptions

description: Amazon Web Services publishes a Post-Event Summary when an issue has broad and significant customer impact, such as failure of a large share of infrastructure in a region. Each summary describes what happened, the scope of the event, the chain of contributing causes, the recovery timeline and the changes AWS will make. The page lists events from April 2011 to October 2025, including the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) disruptions of Amazon S3 in February 2017, AWS Lambda in June 2023 and Amazon DynamoDB in October 2025, and an Amazon EC2 and EBS event in the EU West region in August 2014, as well as earlier power and cooling failures in data centres. Summaries are kept online for at least five years. Coverage: AWS regions worldwide, only the largest events, 2011 to 2025. Format and access: web pages, free to read. Caveats: few events, written by the provider, with timelines in local text, not structured fields; smaller incidents appear only on the AWS Health Dashboard. Simulation uses: failure chains and recovery timelines for cloud and data-centre dependency models, cascading effects of regional outages on dependent services, and scenario design for resilience exercises. Related records: the Azure and Google Cloud incident archives are the counterparts for other providers, and the Cloud Uptime Archive turns status reports into failure traces.
